subject: Leadership summary: buying conditions, risk contingencies & procurement path for QuantaMed
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stone <rachel.stone@quantamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Leadership summary: buying conditions, risk contingencies & procurement path for QuantaMed

Hi Rachel — thank you again for carving out time today. Quick written summary from our side to make sure the leadership team is aligned on the buying conditions and next steps. Please correct anything I miss.

High-level business goals you shared:
- Reduce model-hosting costs for patient-facing documentation generation by ~35% while keeping P95 latency under 350ms
- Centralize inference for multiple product teams into a single controlled runtime for auditability
- Shorten model refresh cycle from 8 weeks to 2–3 weeks for safety/regulatory updates

Primary pain & risk drivers:
1) Current spend volatility with burst traffic during open enrollment — finance needs predictability.
2) Auditability & data residency — Infosec requires KMS/HSM integration and per-request audit logs for PHI-handling flows.
3) Capacity & fallback — product teams can’t tolerate latency spikes; they need automatic fallbacks to lower-cost variants that preserve safety constraints.

Proposed leadership-facing outcomes we discussed:
- Procurement path: standard SOW with a 12-month committed pool (Dedicated) + burst contract for spikes.
- Risk contingencies: SOC 2 attestation delivered + optional on-prem packaging for air-gapped subsystems (if legal requires).
- Decision checkpoints: internal decision by Nov 24 (CFO sign-off), pilot start Dec 6, production by Feb 1.

Immediate asks / next steps (action owners):
- Rachel / QuantaMed: confirm procurement timeline and identify the procurement contact (James listed during call) — Rachel to confirm by EOD 11/04.
- QuantaMed: share any template procurement/contract terms (procurement-intake form) — James or legal.
- Redwood (Diego): share cost estimate and SOC 2 summary, include an optional pilot configuration for the dedicated pool.
- Redwood (Karthik): prepare a short technical annex on KMS/HSM options and fallback routing.

Attachments I’ll include in the follow-up: redwood-cost-estimate-qtm-v1.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf, procurement-intake-quantamed.docx.

Please reply with any clarifications and confirm the decision checkpoint cadence above. Happy to summarize this into a one-pager for your CFO if helpful.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-cost-estimate-qtm-v1.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Leadership summary: buying conditions, risk contingencies & procurement path for QuantaMed

Diego — thanks for the thorough summary. That aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side:

- Procurement timeline: CFO asked for an internal review the week of Nov 22; Nov 24 as a target sign date is realistic if legal clears the contract by then.
- Compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short description of per-request auditing capabilities. Can you attach the SOC 2 summary (not the full report) and call out what logs are available by default?
- On-prem: this is a fallback ask. We’d prefer VPC/private deployment but will escalate on-prem if legal requests it as a condition.

Looping in James (procurement) — James, we’ll need your procurement intake form and any standard PO terms.

Also, we may want a one-page that our CFO can read; please flag any financial levers (committed pool discounts, pilot credits).

Best,
Rachel Stone
Head of Product Engineering
QuantaMed

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the quick confirmation. Per your asks I’ve attached the cost estimate and SOC 2 summary; below are the specific callouts for the CFO one-pager and procurement.

CFO one-pager highlights (for quick-read):
- Unit economics: committed pool pricing (monthly committed tokens) vs on-demand; estimated blended unit cost reduction ~32% at the proposed 12-mo commit.
- Predictability: committed pool + capped burst reduces monthly spend variance and gives pre-negotiated burst rates.
- Pilot credits: 2-week pilot with capped token volume and a one-time $20k credit toward pilot overages for contract sign within 30 days.

Compliance & risk callouts for legal/procurement:
- SOC 2: summary attached (redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf). We provide request-level audit logs (request id, model variant, timestamp, region, tokens processed, KMS envelope ID) and can stream logs to a customer-owned endpoint or S3.
- KMS/HSM: offer KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) and customer-managed keys; see technical annex (Karthik will send).
- Fallbacks: automatic model routing to a quantized, lower-cost variant with identical safety filters; worst-case latency delta < 120ms for bulk inference paths.

Procurement intake (James): I’ve attached a filled procurement-intake-quantamed.docx as a starting point. If legal needs standard MSA redlines, please share and we’ll triage.

Action items (revised):
- James: share PO terms + any non-standard procurement info by 11/10 so we can align legal.
- Rachel: confirm Nov 24 decision checkpoint for CFO.
- Karthik: technical annex for KMS/fallback (deliver by 11/06).
- Diego (me): send CFO one-pager and updated estimate (done, attached).

Attachments: redwood-cost-estimate-qtm-v1.pdf; redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf; procurement-intake-quantamed.docx

All — quick internal note up front: confidential for QuantaMed leadership review only.

Diego / Rachel — I consolidated the call notes for our CFO deck and wanted to call out the gating items that will determine discount thresholds and negotiation posture:

1) Committed volume banding — CFO typically approves higher discounts once committed spend > $1.2M ARR (we should surface the ARR-equivalent in the one-pager).
2) SOC 2 evidence vs full report — legal often wants an SOC 2 report under NDA; offer summary now and full report on NDA.
3) Payment terms — QuantaMed’s standard 60-day net is a potential point of negotiation; our standard is 30-net or prepay for committed pools.

Recommended negotiation path (internal):
- Offer 12-mo committed pool at proposed price with a 45-day decision window for pilot credit redemption.
- If procurement pushes 60-day terms, move commercial to require a short-term credit facility or increase price by a small uplift to offset payment risk.
- Keep on-prem as escalation path (priced separately) — default to VPC/private deployment for speed.

Diego — I’ll draft the CFO one-pager with ARR-equivalent and the discount matrix. Please confirm the final committed pool numbers you used in the estimate (so I match them in the matrix).

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
